headline: Computational models couple microscale mechanics to tissue and cell-shape outcomes
label: Mechanical Models Of Cell Behavior
summary: Recent model-based studies link microscale mechanical and electrical rules to cell shape, migration, nuclear translocation, and tissue necking.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these four published computational studies is a physically explicit model in which local mechanical or biophysical rules are coupled to an emergent cell- or tissue-scale readout. Basement membrane collagen IV turnover and stress relaxation are linked to epithelial cell shape through multiscale modeling and molecular dynamics. Vertex simulations and a mean-field constitutive model relate epithelial tissue necking to cellular topological transitions and defects. A geometric surface PDE treats the plasma membrane and nuclear envelope as evolving energetic surfaces that reproduce microfluidic confinement during nuclear translocation. The electrotaxis and mechanotaxis study examines how electric fields and substrate stiffness gradients interact to direct migration. What is new is the explicit coupling of a specific microscale process to a defined outcome in each case, with all four relying on model-based analysis rather than experimental demonstration within the items.
